searchText: Is there any reason we have withdrawals specced to withdraw any balance above > 32 eth and not considering if a validator is offline? Is it an intention to have validators lose their 32 effective balance mark and potentially have a reduced earnings period while they get back to this mark in case the get a withdrawal and are offline, thus dropping the balance below 32 ETH? Scenario: validator is offline with 32.02 ETH and is eligible for a withdrawal. The withdrawal is processed and their balance falls to 32 ETH. In the next epoch they miss an attestation and their balance falls below 32 ETH. A possible solution would be to add a check to the validator status and make sure that the validator is active and online before processing a withdrawal effective balance only drops to 31 if balance reaches 31.75 AFAICR there’s some damping at play ic, didn't recall that Hi team, just wonder what is the approximate timeline for Goerli and Mainnet upgrade for Shanghai? Thanks! Sepolia on Feb 28th. Goerli after that, mainnet after that. My crystal ball says that if everything goes swimmingly well, mainnet by late March / mid April. And, my crystal ball is dusty and cracked. Hi guys , is there a downtime expected for the Shanghai upgrade or will the nodes continue to function during the upgrade . Thanks Should be continuous. That's part of what all the testing is to ensure. Then new geth version 1.11.2 that was released earlier today , is that for goerli or sepolia ? Read the release notes: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/releases/tag/v1.11.2 I read the release notes. Didn’t see a mention of whether this release is for a specific network sepolia or goerli or does it apply to all networks ? V1.11.0 mentioned sepolia > Geth 1.11.2 (Kite's Nest) is a patch-release, fixing a couple of issues with the 1.11 release family. In general, the Goerli fork epoch isn't yet known That should tell you enough. It doesn't explicitly mention networks or support for upcoming forks, so there's nothing in that release related to it. And as you can see 10 messages above, fork dates have not even been decided yet for those networks. Thanks. Just trying to plan ahead and keep the nodes updated for the hard fork.
